name: RSPWWCW World Heavyweight Championship
epitaph: The federation's own top prize, contested across at least nine reigns through 1997 and carried by the fed's own operator across both the opening and closing reigns this collection's holdings attest.
notes: Reconstructed from 138 dated ring-announcer receipts extracted from the fed's own shows.

name: RSPWWCW Intergender Championship
epitaph: The fed's own signature belt: men and women compete for it on equal terms, and across 1997 it changed hands more often than the world title.

name: RSPWWCW Television Championship
epitaph: Inherited from the 1996 predecessor "RSPW Television Title" and defended through the end of this collection's own 1997 holdings, with its belt still referenced by a sibling fed a year later.

name: RSPWWCW Tag Team Championship
epitaph: Defended across at least five reigns in 1997, including the fed's best-documented single angle -- a staged forfeiture press conference complete with a 1-900 hotline teaser -- and ending the collection's own holdings in a genuinely unresolved chain.
notes: Reconstructed from dated ring-announcer receipts; the August-December 1997 stretch is registered as partially unresolved rather than guessed, per the dossier digest's own finding.

name: RSPWWCW Cruiserweight Championship
epitaph: Created by four-man tournament at the fed's own January 1997 pay-per-view and defended across at least eight reigns through the rest of the year.

name: RSPWWCW Women's Championship
epitaph: Defended across at least six reigns through 1997, its own storylines tied closely to the fed's founding heel stable, the Creatures Of The Night.
notes: Reconstructed from dated ring-announcer receipts; one change carries no recoverable holder name and is not recorded as a row -- see the wing's accession digest.

name: RSPWWCW Extreme Bandwidth Championship
epitaph: The fed's own invention and best joke, created inside the dossier year and named for the very thing its critics accused the fed of wasting.
notes: This pass's own slice finds the shorter "Extreme Championship"/"Extreme Title" name used consistently and exclusively for the remainder of 1997: John Henry calls it "the World champion and the Extreme Champion" at World War IV (23 Nov, msg_id EmGIN266LyQJ); John Henry again congratulates Alex Demchuk "for winning the oldest belt in internet wrestling, the EXTREME Championship" at RawNitro Is War from St. Louis (15 Dec, msg_id 5NeVMCaqTSAJ); and the Boorcade preview at RawNitro Is War from North Pole previews "The Extreme Title... up for grabs as Alex the Hitman Demchuk defends" (22 Dec, msg_id WVqfpmzKrtEJ).

name: RSPWWCW European Championship
epitaph: First attested at the 2001 Regal Rumble, already the sitting Television-style provincial title, changing hands once in the held record: Tehawk to Alex Cain, both reigns dated within the same broadcast.
notes: No document earlier than 29 June 2001 attests this title in the held record; how or when Tehawk won it is not recorded.
